title: Split String - Parsing Text
description: Use Split String to parse CSV data and extract individual values.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Sensor data is coming in CSV format: 'Navigation,Online,75'. We need to split it into separate fields. String library's Split String turns text into lists."
story.context: Splitting strings is fundamental for parsing logs, CSV files, configuration data, and any delimited text.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! You split the CSV line into a list of three values. Now we can access each field individually. Text parsing is essential for data extraction."

instructions: Create *** Settings *** section with Library    String
hints: Separator can be comma, space, pipe, etc.
String library must be imported in Settings
solution:
*** Settings ***
Library    String

*** Test Cases ***
Parse Sensor Data
    ${raw_data}=    Set Variable    Navigation,Online,75
    Log    Raw data: ${raw_data}
    @{fields}=    Split String    ${raw_data}    ,
    Log Many    @{fields}
    ${system}=    Set Variable    ${fields}[0]
    ${status}=    Set Variable    ${fields}[1]
    ${power}=    Set Variable    ${fields}[2]
    Log    System: ${system}, Status: ${status}, Power: ${power}
    Should Be Equal    ${system}    Navigation
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    Online

theory.title: Exercise 4.2.1: Split String
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Text data often comes delimited—CSV files, log entries, configuration lines. Split String breaks text into list items at delimiter boundaries. It's like cutting a string into pieces."

Split String

Convert delimited text into list:

Library    String

${text}=    Set Variable    apple,banana,orange
@{fruits}=    Split String    ${text}    ,
# Result: [apple, banana, orange]

Common Separators:

  • Comma: CSV data (,)
  • Space: Word separation
  • Pipe: Alternative delimiter (|)
  • Tab: TSV data (\t)
  • Newline: Line-by-line (\n)

Example: Log Parsing

*** Settings ***
Library    String

*** Test Cases ***
Parse Log Entry
    ${log}=    Set Variable    2025-10-04 14:30:15 ERROR System failure
    @{parts}=    Split String    ${log}    ${SPACE}    max_split=3
    ${date}=    Set Variable    ${parts}[0]
    ${time}=    Set Variable    ${parts}[1]
    ${level}=    Set Variable    ${parts}[2]
    ${message}=    Set Variable    ${parts}[3]
    Log    Error at ${date} ${time}: ${message}

⚠️ Split String Tips

  • Returns list (use @{variable})
  • Separator is literal (case-sensitive)
  • Use max_split to limit splits
  • Empty fields create empty string items
  • Great for: CSV, logs, configuration, delimited data
